title: Worker orphan recovery should use configured PR base branch
body:
## Problem

Workers repeatedly failed to solve a straightforward managed-repo issue because the recovery/orphan path kept producing `WORKER_BRANCH_ORPHAN` comments instead of an actionable PR.

Evidence from an interactive managed-repo recovery:

- The issue is a small two-file code change plus tests.
- Multiple worker attempts pushed branches but reported `worker_branch_orphan`.
- The recovery comment told maintainers to run `gh pr create --head <branch> --base main`, but the repo's required integration branch is `develop`.
- The same orphan pattern repeated across branch names until dispatch was held by repeated-orphan loop detection.
- Manual interactive recovery succeeded by using a linked worktree, opening a PR against `develop`, waiting for green checks, and merging.

## Why this matters

This is a first-time-success gap in aidevops orchestration, not a task difficulty problem. A worker that has already pushed a viable branch should either open a PR to the repository's configured base branch or produce a recovery command that does so. Recommending `main` for a `develop`-based repository creates a repeated failure loop and burns worker attempts.

## Suggested fix

Make the worker orphan/recovery path use the repository's configured PR base branch everywhere it creates or suggests PRs.

Likely areas to inspect:

- worker branch orphan telemetry/comment generation
- dispatch recovery that emits `WORKER_BRANCH_ORPHAN`
- any fallback `gh pr create --base main` template
- repo configuration lookup for default branch vs PR target branch

## Acceptance criteria

- For repos configured with `develop` as the PR target, orphan recovery comments suggest `--base develop`, not `--base main`.
- The same configured base is used when automation attempts to open the PR itself.
- A regression test covers a repo whose default branch is not the PR target branch.
- Repeated orphan loop detection includes a next action that either opens a PR against the configured base or explicitly says no commits exist to PR.

## Verification

- Run the helper/unit tests that cover worker orphan comment generation.
- Add a fixture for a `develop`-based managed repo and assert the emitted `gh pr create` command targets `develop`.
- If there is an integration helper for dispatch recovery, run it against a dry-run fixture with a pushed branch and confirm the PR base is `develop`.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status.

   Linux / systemd user timers:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user status aidevops-stats-wrapper.timer --no-pager
   systemctl --user status aidevops-stats-wrapper.service --no-pager
   systemctl --user list-timers --all --no-pager 'aidevops*'
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/.config/systemd/user/aidevops-stats-wrapper.*
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash

   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops.sh/issues/71 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

- **macOS missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.

Add a small POST/PATCH helper for issue creation, modelled on `github_url_request`. - `NEW: .github/workflows/services-sync-check.yml` — model on `.github/workflows/update-site-stats.yml` (checkout@v5, `GITHUB_TOKEN` env, `python3 scripts/...`), but with its own `permissions: {contents: read, issues: write}`, no Pages steps, and no `github-pages` concurrency group. Site edits happen in the auto-dispatched worker PR, never in CI. - **Existing verification/tests:** none cover services; the repo has no Python test suite. Verify through the CLI dry-run and the `workflow_dispatch` run below. Do not add test infrastructure. - **Schemas/config:** `data/services-sync.json` (new). Don't add it to the Pages `_site` copy list in `update-site-stats.yml`; it isn't a public asset. - **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `docs.html` is auto-synced from upstream README. Exclude it. - **Migrations/backfills:** the one-time mapping seed in this PR. - **Cleanup/rollback paths:** delete the three new files and revert the DESIGN.md line. There is no persistent state outside Git. ### Implementation Steps 1. `load_site_entries()` — parse `#services` `
  • ` link text exactly as in the Quick-Start. Unique names are the count; duplicates across categories (FluentCRM appears in `Business & Payments` and `Email`) must not inflate it. 2. `load_tree(sha)` — upstream recursive tree for HEAD and for `baseline_commit`. Fail the job, don't file an issue, if either tree is `truncated`. 3. Compute findings: - `added` = `.md` blobs under `candidate_prefixes` present at HEAD but not at baseline, excluding basenames `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `index.md`, and not in any `services` value or `acknowledged`. - `removed` = mapped paths absent at HEAD. - `changed` = mapped paths in the compare file list since baseline whose current frontmatter `description:` or first `# ` heading matches the deprecation keywords (fetch with `raw_github_text(path)`). - `unmapped` = site names missing from `services`, plus mapping keys that are no longer on the site. - `count_claims` = each claim location whose number is not `floor(unique/10)*10`. 4. For each `added` candidate, include its frontmatter `description:` in the report so triage is cheap. Cap it at 60 candidates and state the overflow count. 5. Output: always write a Markdown summary to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` when set, and to stdout. `--dry-run` never writes to GitHub. 6. Filing, only when findings exist and not `--dry-run`: - Search open issues in this repo for the marker ``. If one is open, do nothing (a worker may be mid-fix). The next run after it closes catches anything newer. - Otherwise create one issue: - Title: `Sync site services list with upstream aidevops ()`. - Labels: `enhancement,auto-dispatch,tier:standard,origin:worker`. These all exist in this repo. - Body: the findings, a worker-ready `## What / ## How / ## Acceptance` block embedded in the script, the marker, and the upstream HEAD SHA to advance `baseline_commit` to. 7. The embedded resolution instructions for the drift-fixing worker must say: - Follow DESIGN.md "Services and integrations links": official brand URL sourced from project metadata and confirmed to resolve, never guessed; GitHub-only projects link to GitHub; no status badges; retired services removed. - Update `index.html` and `data/services-sync.json` together. Add a triaged-out candidate to `acknowledged` with a reason. - Update the count claims when they are listed. - Set `baseline_commit` to the SHA in the issue. - Verify with `python3 scripts/check_services_sync.py --dry-run --head `, which must report no findings. 8. CLI flags: `--dry-run`, `--head SHA` (default upstream `main` HEAD), `--baseline SHA` (default from JSON). They make the verification below reproducible. ### Hazards and Compatibility - **Concurrency/atomicity:** one open drift issue at a time (marker check), so a worker is never mid-fix while the body changes. A run racing a just-merged fix at worst re-files once. Acceptable, and it self-corrects on the next run. - **Migration/rollback:** no persisted CI state. Rollback = revert the PR. - **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an interactive services-list refresh (Closte removed; Apple container, Firecracker microVMs, Gonicus Bubbles and Buzz added; FluentCRM also under Email; `.service-soon` retired) may merge before or after this work. - If it has merged when you start, seed those entries too. - If not, don't edit `index.html` for it. The first scheduled run will report those names under `unmapped`, which is the intended self-healing path. - This task shouldn't touch `index.html` at all, so there's no conflict with that PR. - **Idempotency/retry:** reuse `urlopen_with_retries` (it already retries 403/429/5xx). About 4 REST calls plus at most 60 raw fetches per run. Exit non-zero on API failure without filing. - **Partial failure/recovery:** issue creation is the only write, and it happens last, after all findings are computed. - **Public repository — no keys:** this repo and its Actions logs are public. Never commit keys, tokens, credentials, or `.env` files. Never add repository or environment secrets, PATs, or deploy keys. The workflow uses only the built-in, short-lived Actions token (`secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, scoped by the workflow `permissions:` block), which is not a stored key. The script reads it from the environment only when filing an issue. `--dry-run` must work with no token at all. Never print token values, `Authorization` headers, or raw API error bodies that might echo them to stdout, logs, `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, or issue bodies. - **Trust boundary:** `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. The issue author will be `github-actions[bot]`. The maintainer gate treats `github-actions[bot]` issues with an `origin:worker` label as trusted (t2451, `maintainer-gate-reusable.yml`). If the first real drift issue is still held for maintainer review, report that in the PR. Never weaken the gate, and never add a PAT or cross-repo token. ### Verification Before Dispatch ```bash python3 -m py_compile scripts/check_services_sync.py python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('data/services-sync.json'))" # Dry runs need NO token: upstream is public and a run uses ~4 REST calls (well inside the 60/hour unauthenticated limit). # Do not export, paste, or print any token for these commands. # Clean state: seeded mapping at upstream HEAD -> no removed/unmapped findings (count_claims may legitimately report 140+ vs 150+ until the site copy is updated) python3 scripts/check_services_sync.py --dry-run # Detection proof: an older baseline surfaces added candidates python3 scripts/check_services_sync.py --dry-run --baseline # Removal proof: a head from before the Buzz team-interface doc existed reports Buzz under removed python3 scripts/check_services_sync.py --dry-run --head # No credentials committed anywhere in the change ! git diff origin/main --name-only | xargs rg -n "ghp_|github_pat_|gho_|ghs_|ghu_|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY|Bearer [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{20,}" ``` - **Surface mapping:** py_compile/JSON load prove the new files parse; the three dry runs prove the clean, added and removed paths without GitHub writes. After merge, one `workflow_dispatch` run proves permissions and the step summary. - **Broad verification trigger:** not required. ### Files Scope **Hard boundaries:** - Do not edit `index.html` services entries, `docs.html`, or `update-site-stats.yml`. - Public repo: no keys, tokens, credentials or `.env` files in any committed file. - No new repository or environment secrets, PATs, or deploy keys. - The only credential is the built-in Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN`. - `scripts/check_services_sync.py` - `data/services-sync.json` - `.github/workflows/services-sync-check.yml` - `DESIGN.md` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `python3 scripts/check_services_sync.py --dry-run` against upstream HEAD reports zero `removed` and zero `unmapped` findings once the mapping is seeded. ```yaml verify: method: bash run: "python3 -m py_compile scripts/check_services_sync.py && python3 -c \"import json; d=json.load(open('data/services-sync.json')); assert d['schema']==1 and len(d['baseline_commit'])==40 and d['services']\"" ``` - [ ] With `--baseline` set to an older upstream SHA, the dry run lists new candidate docs with their frontmatter descriptions. With `--head` set before a mapped doc existed, that entry appears under `removed`. - [ ] With findings and no `--dry-run`, exactly one issue is created with labels `enhancement,auto-dispatch,tier:standard,origin:worker` and the `aidevops:generator=services-sync-check` marker. A second run while it is open creates nothing. - [ ] Negative: CI never commits to or edits `index.html`. The workflow has no `contents: write`. ```yaml verify: method: codebase pattern: "contents: write" path: ".github/workflows/services-sync-check.yml" expect: absent ``` - [ ] Negative (public repo): the workflow references no secret other than the built-in `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, and no committed file contains a key, token or private key. ```yaml verify: method: bash run: "! rg -n 'secrets\\.' .github/workflows/services-sync-check.yml | rg -v 'secrets\\.GITHUB_TOKEN' && ! rg -n 'ghp_|github_pat_|gho_|ghs_|ghu_|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY' scripts data .github DESIGN.md" ``` - [ ] `python3 scripts/check_services_sync.py --dry-run` succeeds with `GITHUB_TOKEN` unset. - [ ] DESIGN.md documents the mapping file and the same-PR update rule. ## Context & Decisions - **Why the check lives in this repo, not upstream aidevops:** the site list, its copy rules (DESIGN.md) and a daily CI that already reads the upstream tree all live here.   • `:** it keeps `index.html` untouched, so this work can't conflict with in-flight list edits, and the mapping stays machine-readable. - **Why a baseline cursor:** about 1,500 existing upstream docs are mostly framework-internal. Flagging only docs added since the cursor avoids a huge initial ignore list. Advancing the cursor in the fix PR is the versioned "reviewed up to here" record. - **Why no auto-edits in CI:** choosing whether a doc is a listable service, its category and its official URL are judgement calls reserved for the worker (DESIGN.md forbids guessed vendor URLs). - **Non-goals:** - Detecting services the maintainer stopped using while the upstream doc still exists (e.g. Closte). ## What

Landing-page refresh for aidevops.sh, implemented interactively with the maintainer. It covers the approved copy, a new public-proof section, a brand-linked services list, and a live-accurate release badge.

## Why

- The hero version badge usually trailed the latest aidevops release by one version. The upstream `update-website-docs.yml` push-triggered docs sync deploys the site a few minutes before each GitHub release is published, and its release-triggered run finds no `docs.html` change, so it doesn't redeploy.

- **`#github-memory` proof section:**
  - Five linked metrics.
  - A who/what/why trail.
  - API-limit and self-improvement notes.
  - The copy ends "every receipt is built in public."
- **Services:**
  - Each name links to the provider's brand site.
  - `soon` badges and `.service-soon` removed.
  - Closte removed.
  - Added:
    - Apple container, Firecracker microVMs and Gonicus Bubbles, after OrbStack.
    - OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go and NanoGPT.
    - NostrVPN.
    - FluentCRM, also listed under Email.
    - Buzz (buzz.xyz), at the top of Team Chat.
  - Count claims: 154 unique services, rounded down to "150+" in the hero, the capability pill and the JSON-LD.
- **Stats:**
  - `scripts/update_site_stats.py` refreshes the inventory, release, activity and maintainer stats, plus the social-graph metrics and the JSON-LD version fallback.

- **`DESIGN.md`:** records the approved copy, the landing-page structure, the proof and count rules, the services link rules, and the version-badge rationale. The shared Brand core block is left byte-identical with `marcusquinn/aidevops`.

- [ ] The desktop and mobile previews show the new copy with no mid-phrase wraps and no page errors.

- [ ] `node --check script.js`, JSON validity and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] After merge, the Pages deploy succeeds and the live site serves the new copy, `script.js?v=7` and the latest release badge.

- #170: 404 hover contrast (separate worker task; may touch the `404.html` cache-buster).

The open-source OpenCode plugin for AI Git workflow automation." They currently say "…autonomous project delivery across code, infrastructure, SEO, and services" and "Give your AI assistant DevOps superpowers".
